liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **New Speedway Boogie** (3 reviews): Reviewer thinks this version sounds identical to the New Speedway Boogie on the Fallout from the Phil Zone release; Reviewer points to Bobby and Jerry trading licks during Speedway [6][8][16]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the nicest Uncle John's Band they have heard [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Wake Up Little Susie**: rare: 9 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-05-01.sbd.miller.95683.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 126 min; rated 4.62/5 by 37 [1]
- **gd70-05-01.sbd.clugston.5465.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 89 min; rated 4.22/5 by 32 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording notably clear; Reviewer describes the sound as stellar [7][16]
- **gd1970-05-01.sbd.gans-miller.85322.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 13 songs; 89 min; rated 4.3/5 by 10 [2]
- **gd1970-05-01.sbd.unknown.93.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 3 songs; 12 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]

## Around the show

- The New Riders portion of the show is missing from this tape, which the reviewer laments [16]
- Part of the acoustic set featured members of the New Riders [1]
- The acoustic set was followed by a New Riders set with Garcia on pedal steel, including Honky Tonk Women [3]
- The show closed with an electric Dead set running from Drums into Not Fade Away through Turn On Your Lovelight [3]
- Reviewer rates the sound quality and performance as on a level with the following day's show [5]
- Reviewer expects the 5/2 show to be more substantial than this night, though they hadn't yet heard it [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-05-01.sbd.miller.95683.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Source 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD Source 2: SBD ->Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD Source 3: SBD -> Master Reel -> Reel-> Dat -> Sonic Solutions ->… [1]. Also: Three sources are combined: Deep Elem Blues to Cumberland Blues, then The Race Is On to mid-Drums, then mid-Drums to the end; David Gans supplied sources 2 and 3; Joe B. Jones helped with pitch correction [1]
- **gd70-05-01.sbd.clugston.5465.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Soundboard [3]. Also: These songs were long believed to be from 5/19/70 at Washington U in Missouri, a show that apparently never happened; Dick Lavatna later concluded the material was likely from 5/1/70 at Alfred; some reels reportedly turned up under a stage at Merrimac CC on 5/14/70; Master soundboard reel, partly via reel to reel, then DAT, Sonic Solutions and CDR; transferred and shortened to SHN by Scott Clugston [3][15]
- **gd1970-05-01.sbd.gans-miller.85322.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by David Gans and Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD [2]
- **gd1970-05-01.sbd.unknown.93.sbeok.shnf**: source: soundboard [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by lostlivedead.blogspot.com: [The Grateful Dead in Upstate and Central New York 1969-79 ('Til Your Night Job Pays)](https://lostlivedead.blogspot.com/2020/05/the-grateful-dead-in-upstate-and.html) [23]
